ic_name: HDMI / DVI TMDS (TI TFP410 PanelBus Digital Transmitter — subset)

clock_and_reset_waveform.POR_release: After Power-On Reset, devices must release both SDA and SCL (drive HIGH-Z) before any transaction.

bit_transfer_waveform.rule: Data on SDA must be stable while SCL is HIGH (data valid window). SDA may change while SCL is LOW (change-of-data window).
bit_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 4 — Bit transfer on the I2C-bus

start_stop_waveform.start_S: SDA HIGH→LOW transition while SCL HIGH
start_stop_waveform.stop_P: SDA LOW→HIGH transition while SCL HIGH
start_stop_waveform.repeated_start_Sr: Same as S; keeps bus busy without intervening P

data_transfer_waveform.byte_unit: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock = 9 SCL pulses per byte
data_transfer_waveform.ack_position: On the 9th SCL pulse; receiver pulls SDA LOW
data_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 6 — Data transfer on the I2C-bus

timing_parameters_high_speed_mode.drive: Open-drain with current-source pull-up; SDA push-pull on HIGH

clock_stretching_waveform: Slave holds SCL LOW after a byte to extend the byte period; master enters wait state.
arbitration_waveform: While SCL HIGH, each master compares SDA actual to SDA driven; master that drove HIGH while bus is LOW loses arbitration immediately.
synchronization_waveform: SCL = wired-AND of all masters' SCL outputs; final LOW period = longest LOW, final HIGH period = shortest HIGH.

clock_waveform.leading_edge: EDGE=1 → rising edge of IDCK+; EDGE=0 → falling.
clock_waveform.differential_clock_crossover: Differential mode only available in low-swing mode (V_REF ≤ 0.9 V).
clock_waveform.dual_edge_mode: 12-bit DATA[11:0] latched on BOTH edges of IDCK+.

output_tmds_waveform.step_1_power_up: PD=1 (via pin or register) → PLL begins locking (few µs).
output_tmds_waveform.step_2_pll_lock: 10× PLL locks to IDCK; serializer bit clock = 10 × IDCK frequency.
output_tmds_waveform.step_3_encode_pixel: Each IDCK period: encode 3 × 8-bit pixels (R, G, B) → 3 × 10-bit TMDS characters.
output_tmds_waveform.step_4_serialize: Each 10-bit symbol shifted out per channel at bit rate = 10 × IDCK (LSB-first on the wire).
output_tmds_waveform.step_5_differential_swing: Each TX+ / TX- pair drives 400-600 mV single-ended (V_SWING), set by R_TFADJ.
output_tmds_waveform.step_6_de_low_blanking: When DE=low, encoder emits control characters: TX0 = {VSYNC,HSYNC} code, TX1 = {CTL[1],0} code, TX2 = {CTL[3],CTL[2]} code with CTL[3]=0.
output_tmds_waveform.step_7_de_high_active: When DE=high, encoder emits transition-minimised + DC-balanced video characters per channel.
output_tmds_waveform.step_8_disable: PD=0 or TDIS=1 gates driver to V_OFF (both TX+ and TX- pulled to AV_DD).

single_edge_falling_idr.description: Setup / hold of DATA, DE, VSYNC, HSYNC to IDCK+ falling edge (BSEL=1, DSEL=0, DKEN=0, EDGE=0).

single_edge_rising_idr.description: Setup / hold of DATA, DE, VSYNC, HSYNC to IDCK+ rising edge (BSEL=1, DSEL=0, DKEN=0, EDGE=1).

dual_edge_id.description: Setup / hold of DATA, DE, VSYNC, HSYNC to BOTH IDCK+ edges in 12-bit dual-edge mode (BSEL=0, DSEL=1, DKEN=0).

deskew_waveform.formula: t_CD = (DK[3:1] - 4) × t_STEP, where t_STEP ≈ 350 ps; data can be latched 4·t_STEP early to 3·t_STEP late relative to IDCK edge.
deskew_waveform.purpose: Compensate IDCK ↔ DATA arrival skew at the TFP410 input; clock itself is NOT delayed, only the data latching window.

i2c_waveform.data_transition: SDA changes only while SCL LOW.
i2c_waveform.ack_at_9th_clock: Receiver pulls SDA LOW on 9th clock.

tmds_character_serialization.format: Per-channel: 10 bits per IDCK period; LSB-first on the wire.
tmds_character_serialization.channel_independence: Each channel maintains its own running disparity.
tmds_character_serialization.control_vs_video: DE=low → control character; DE=high → video character; 10-bit code emitted in 1 IDCK period.

general_timing_rule: All TMDS output bit times derived from bit clock = 10 × f_IDCK. Per channel, 10 bits per IDCK period. IDCK ↔ DATA setup/hold must be met. PLL multiplies IDCK by 10×; on-chip 1.8 V regulators + bypass caps reduce PLL noise.
